newsitem.title: USA: Jones backs Q3, Q4 EPS estimates in $0.30 range.
newsitem.headline: Jones backs Q3, Q4 EPS estimates in $0.30 range.

text.p: Jones Medical Industries Inc said Monday it is comfortable with Wall Street analysts' earnings estimates of about $0.30 per share for both the third and fourth quarters.

"We're very, very comfortable ... with third and fourth quarter estimates that are in the $0.30 range and we've not encouraged analysts to lower those," said Jones Medical chairman and chief executive Dennis Jones in a teleconference.
Shares in the St. Louis-based firm were off 15-3/8 to 28 on heavy volume of nearly 13 million shares in late trading.

Shares fell on the company's announcement late Thursday that it expects second-quarter earnings to be about $0.20 per share, or about $0.08 per share less than the consensus First Call estimate of $0.28 per share.
The shortfall stemmed from aggressive wholesale buying of two of its top-selling drugs -- Tapazole and Levoxyl -- ahead of an April 1 price hike, the company said.
The price increase was announced March 24. "In retrospect, we probably gave (wholesalers) too much opportunity to take advantage of some bargain buying in late March," Jones said.
"We understand what is happening and we believe that third and fourth quarter 1997 will not have the dynamics of the two quarters that we've just discussed," Jones said.

He said sales on the second quarter were $27.5 million. On the quarterly earnings estimate, Jones said, "What we've outlined is a worst-case ... There's a possibility that they might be a tad better than $0.20 per share."
On Wall Street estimates for 1997, Jones said, "Obviously, with an $0.08 or so shortfall in the second quarter, their 1997 estimates will undoubtedly come down about that amount."
Insiders own more than 20 percent of the company, Jones said. "No one suffered more today than my wife and I and our officers ... Today was not a happy day at Jones," he said.
